title: Pavlova
description: Crisp meringue shell with a soft center, dried low and slow.
beforeYouStart: Egg whites at room temperature; bowl and whisk totally free of fat or yolk
No superfine sugar? Pulse granulated sugar in a food processor a few times
Line the sheet with parchment or a silicone mat; don't grease it
Save the 4 yolks for lemon curd

items.do: Heat the oven to 350°F. (You'll drop it to 200°F the moment the pavlova goes in.)
Whip the whites on medium-high to soft peaks.
Add the sugar in two parts, beating about 30 sec after each. Then go to high speed.
items.cue: Glossy, stiff peaks that don't move when the whisk is held upright

items.do: Beat in the vanilla for 1 minute. If the peaks have softened, keep beating.
Gently fold in the cream of tartar and cornstarch with a spatula.
Spread into an 8–9 in circle with tall edges and a clear hollow in the center. Swirl peaks with the back of a spoon if you like.
Put it in the oven and immediately turn the heat down to 200°F. Rotate once if spots start browning; otherwise keep the door shut.
items.cue: Firm and dry to the touch, and still pale

items.do: Turn the oven off and let the pavlova cool completely inside it. The slow cool keeps cracking down.
Right before serving, pile on whipped cream, curd, and fruit. Slice and serve.

items: Plain, cooled shell keeps up to 2 days at room temp in an airtight container
Best eaten right after topping; doesn't freeze well
Acid: 1 tsp white vinegar, cider vinegar, or lemon juice instead of cream of tartar. The source notes a little more spread with liquid acid.
Minis: portion into 6 nests with centers hollowed. Same 350°F start, then ~35–40 min at 200°F (readers report they may need longer).
Humid days slow the whipping and drying; plan extra oven time
